result:
I graded your second attempt (`submissions/s2.json`) and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. You got three correct, two partial and one wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | Correct | The model writes a request and the program runs the tool. Your first attempt had this wrong. |
| q3 | Wrong (M6) | You chose "it will eventually fix the bug". A stuck agent repeats itself, so it needs a stopping condition like a step limit. A step limit also caps the cost of one request. |
| q4 | Partial (M4) | Your 4 is right, but you wrote that the model "runs" each tool. The model only requests a tool, and the program runs it. The count is 3 requests plus 1 answer. |
| q5 | Correct | You gave both halves: the result goes back as the next input, so the model can decide what to do next. |
| q6 | Partial | A tool's name is only part of what the model uses. It picks from the whole description: name, purpose and parameters. |

**What you have down:** the shape of the loop, and that tool results go back in as the model's next input.

**What to work on:**
- The model never runs a tool.
- An agent needs a stopping condition.

**Next step:** Trace one makerspace request on paper, marking each line "model writes" or "program runs". Then add a step limit and say what happens when it is reached.

I also added learning record 0003 and updated `NOTES.md`. I only graded s2, so `submissions/s1.json` is still ungraded.
